title: Lonely Pixel II
summary: In an m x n picture with black 'B' and white 'W' pixels, count the black 'B' pixels that meet these criteria: the pixel is at a position (r, c) where both row r and column c have exactly target black 'B' pixels, and every row with a black 'B' in column c matches row r exactly.
statement: In an m x n picture with black 'B' and white 'W' pixels, count the black 'B' pixels that meet these criteria: the pixel is at a position (r, c) where both row r and column c have exactly target black 'B' pixels, and every row with a black 'B' in column c matches row r exactly.
constraints: Source 533 uses boards up to 200 by 200. This app explicitly supports 1 <= rows, columns <= 500 to cover source 531 as target=1.
The board is rectangular and contains only B (black) or W (white). 1 <= target <= min(rows,columns).
Count black pixels, not rows or columns. A qualifying pixel has exactly target black cells in its row and column, AND every row containing a black pixel in that column is identical in all columns.
hints: Rows that are exactly equal can be grouped together.
A qualifying row pattern must appear target times, have target black positions, and use columns whose total black count is target.
Count row tuples and column black cells; for each row pattern with frequency target and target black cells, add frequency for every qualifying black column.
A column can be spoiled by one black pixel in a different row pattern. Multiply by the number of identical rows because the answer counts pixels.
editorial: For a qualifying pixel, all target black cells in its column belong to identical rows. Hence its row pattern appears exactly target times. Conversely, a pattern with target copies and target black positions qualifies at each black column whose total is target: there can be no extra nonidentical row there. Grouping row tuples and counting columns takes O(rows*columns) time and space. The oracle directly inspects every black pixel and compares all rows contributing to its column without grouped-frequency reasoning.

tests.explanation: Columns 1 and 3 each contain three black pixels in the three identical top rows. All six pixels qualify. Column 4 has four black pixels, so none there qualify.
Return 0: each row and column has two black pixels, but the rows sharing any black column are different. Matching counts alone are not enough.
